title: color_rgba element type check is dead (!ok vs okc) — malformed component silently coerced to 0
detail: The cast's ok value (okc) is never tested; `!ok` reads the outer json.Object cast, always true here. A non-integer element fails the cast, yields n=0, passes the range guard — malformed JSON silently coerces to 0 instead of failing fast (ODN-5).
recommended_fix: Change the guard to `if !okc || n < 0 || n > 255` so a failed json.Integer cast rejects the row instead of defaulting to 0.

title: default_lane range-checked after u8 truncation — out-of-range values wrap into validity (two sites)
detail: u8(jint(...)) truncates mod 256 before the >2 guard: JSON values 256/257/258 wrap to 0/1/2 and pass validation (CWE-681). Both new loaders (packet_types, demand entries) share the flaw; the wrapped lane rides into 3.2's lane data.
recommended_fix: Range-check the i32 before narrowing: dl := jint(...); if dl < 0 || dl > 2 { return ... }; then assign u8(dl). Apply at both sites.

title: set-piece tick fields accept negatives via u64 sign-extension — silent never-fires window
evidence:
sp.start_tick = u64(jint(seo, "start_tick", 0))
					sp.duration_ticks = u64(jint(seo, "duration_ticks", 0))
					sp.forecast_lead_ticks = u64(jint(seo, "forecast_lead_ticks", 0))
					if sp.multiplier < 1 || sp.duration_ticks == 0 {
detail: u64(jint(...)) sign-extends: start_tick -1 becomes 2^64-1 and is accepted (only multiplier<1 and duration==0 are checked). The set-piece then silently never fires (or window arithmetic wraps) — out-of-range input accepted, violating the ODN-5 fail-fast bar.
recommended_fix: Read into i32 first and reject negative start_tick/duration_ticks/forecast_lead_ticks before the u64 cast.
